messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Incident INC-4721 — Potential data residency policy violation detected for tenant 'acme-eu' (alerts: smart-routing fallback -> non-EU region). Pushed to incidents channel and paged Robin (oncall).

Robin (oncall): seeing it. joining.

Robin (oncall): quick summary? what triggered detection?

pagerduty-bot: detection rule `residency.monitor.v1` flagged >20 requests routed to us-east-1 for tenant tag region=EU within 2m.

Jordan (infra): I have a trace: requests came in with region_hint=eu-west-1 but smart-routing decision picked model-quantized-v2 in us-east-1 due to capacity fallback.

Jordan (infra): snippet from routing log: 
```
[2026-07-17T11:05:12Z] req_id=F2b3 routing: tenant=acme-eu route=smart-route policy=cost_aware fallback_allowed=true chosen_region=us-east-1 chosen_variant=model-quant-v2 reason=slot_unavailable_eu
[2026-07-17T11:05:12Z] req_id=F2b3 residency_check=FAIL tenant_region=eu member_region=eu chosen_region=us-east-1
```

Robin (oncall): uh. so fallback_policy allowed region mismatch. that should have been blocked by residency policy.

Sara (SRE): paging in Mike (security) and Olivia (product) for compliance assessment.

Mike (security): on it. do we know if any PII left region? how many requests?

Jordan (infra): estimated 1.2k requests over 3m window, 87 unique sessions. Looks like smart-routing fallback loop: capacity shortage in eu models -> route to cheapest compatible variant -> variant only available in us-east.

Olivia (product): affected tenant is a regulated EU customer under SCCs. this is high severity. we need containment immediately.

Robin (oncall): mitigation plan step 1: disable smart-routing fallback to non-residency regions globally for now. step 2: apply explicit deny rule for tenants with residency tags until policy fix. assigning tasks.

Jordan (infra): doing step 1 now. applying temporary toggle: `platform.smart_routing.allow_cross_region_fallback=false`

deploy-bot: Deploy started: toggle update by jordan — rolling to control plane (3 targets).

Jordan (infra): applied deny rule for tenant acme-eu via routing policy: `residency.enforce.acme-eu = strict` (no cross-region fallback).

Robin (oncall): confirm controls: are new requests now blocked from leaving EU?

Jordan (infra): yes, new traces show chosen_region=eu-west-1 or failover->503 when EU capacity exhausted.

Mike (security): good. next: we need to determine data exfil risk. who can access request payload logs outside EU?

Jordan (infra): logs: request bodies are not stored in hot logs outside EU; KV cache snapshots did replicate to us-east for that variant earlier today — investigating which keys contain PII.

Sara (SRE): starting live grep on cache replication metadata (slow, doing safe reads). will flag keys that look like user content.

Olivia (product): we should notify legal and customer success. I'll open the customer notification draft.

Mike (security): please collect impacted request_ids and time ranges. we'll run a scoped audit and HSM key access check.

Robin (oncall): handoff — I need to hand to Sara for the next hour while I coordinate exec comms. Sara, take primary.

Sara (SRE): taking primary. all tasks consolidated in this thread. I'm running a quick map of affected requests -> data plane nodes.

Sara (SRE): preliminary numbers: ~1.2k requests, ~650 tokenized outputs cached, 12 cache shards in us-east had replicas for tenant prefix `acme-eu/` between 11:03-11:08 UTC.

Mike (security): flagged for incident response. setting severity P1. initiating compliance review.

Jordan (infra): root cause: routing policy precedence bug — `policy.residency` was lower priority than `policy.smart_routing.fallback` if fallback_allowed=true. fix will flip precedence and add a test.

Sara (SRE): mitigation steps completed: toggle off, deny rules applied, affected cache shards locked and snapshot export started for forensic analysis.

deploy-bot: Toggle update completed by jordan — all control plane nodes healthy.

Robin (oncall): good work. Olivia, draft for customer comms? keep wording minimal: acknowledge routing error, containment, we are auditing for data residency exposure, will follow up with findings.

Olivia (product): draft in docs/cust-notify/acme-eu-datarouting.md (private). sharing with legal now.

Mike (security): immediate ask to legal: do we need to notify regulators? hold until audit completes but prep for GDPR timeline.

Sara (SRE): ETA for full audit: 6 hours for fingerprinting and 24h for full content review (if needed). I'll update channel as results come in.

Jordan (infra): PR for permanent fix created: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5182 — change: residency policy precedence + unit tests + e2e for fallback scenarios.

Robin (oncall): assigning postmortem to Jordan + Sara + Mike. Pedro from legal cc'd by Olivia.

Mike (security): noted. preserve all logs and evidence. no data deletion until legal advises.

Sara (SRE): handing off active oncall to Mike (security) for midnight window. I'll remain in thread for followups.

Mike (security): taking handoff. thanks.

Robin (oncall): closing pager escalation for now — containment achieved. keep thread updated with audit artifacts.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-4721 acknowledged and updated: status=contained, severity=P1 -> under review.

Sara (SRE): next updates: forensic snapshot id=fs-20260717-1108, audit ticket INTG-334. will post sanitized findings here in ~6h. :lock:

Olivia (product): customer comms queued. legal reviewed initial draft. awaiting audit detail before sending.

Jordan (infra): PR merged to main; deploy scheduled in 1h to promote fix across regions.

Mike (security): I'll start regulator notification prep templates in parallel.

Robin (oncall): thanks team. good triage. reactions: :thumbsup: :shield:
